name: British Virgin Islands
summary: The British Virgin Islands have no forced heirship, though English-style family provision claims exist. Foreign inheritance rights are disregarded against a BVI trust (Trustee Act s. 83A) and VISTA trusts are available. The Hague Trusts Convention is in force; no foundation law was found.
family_claims: A law firm says BVI law, on the English model, lets spouses, children and dependants apply for reasonable provision from the estate. The statute was not named.
foreign_law_note: BVI land follows BVI law; movables, including shares in BVI companies, follow the law of the deceased's domicile, so a will cannot override forced heirship at the domicile. There is no choice of nationality law.
trust_note: BVI is on the UK's HCCH extension (in force 1 January 1992). Trustee Act (Cap. 303) s. 83A(14), amended 2021, disregards foreign heirship rights over a BVI trust; VISTA allows trusts holding BVI company shares. No foundation law was identified.
open_questions: Family provision statute and eligibility not identified.
Foundation law not confirmed absent; the IFC Review list does not name BVI.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.
